title: Prospective, double-blind, randomised clinical trial on the influence of probiotics on clinical parameters, the oral microbiome, and the local cytokine profile in adolescent patients undergoing orthodontic treatment.
summary:
Probiotics – The “Good” Helpers!
This study compares adjuvant intake of probiotic lozenges (Limosilactobacillus reuteri) with control lozenges (without probiotics). Probiotics are live microorganisms that can have a positive effect on health by promoting the natural balance of microorganisms in the body.
The participants are adolescents aged 12 to 17 who are undergoing orthodontic treatment with fixed appliance. Maintaining oral hygiene can be more challenging after the placement of the fixed appliance, which can lead to increased plaque accumulation and changes in the composition of bacteria in the mouth. These changes can result in gum swelling or bleeding.

This study aims to determine whether adjuvant intake of probiotic versus control lozenges for the first three months after the placement of the fixed appliance results in less gum inflammation. 
We also investigate whether there is a reduction in the release of inflammatory substances and an improvement in the presence of "good" bacteria in the mouth.

The study begins with the placement of the fixed appliance and lasts for six months. Participants are randomly assigned to receive either probiotic or placebo lozenges, which they take twice daily for three months following the placement of the fixed appliance.

Neither the participants nor the treating physicians know which lozenges the participants are taking (double-blind design), ensuring reliable results. Samples to examine the oral microbiota and local cytokine expression are collected during routine orthodontic appointments.
conditions: Fixed orthodontic appliances are used in children and adolescents to correct dental and jaw misalignments. After placement of the fixed appliance, maintaining oral hygiene can become more difficult, leading to the accumulation of dental plaque. This may result in gum inflammation (gingivitis), enamel demineralization (white spots), and changes in the oral microbiome.

interventions.name: Adolescents (age 12–17) undergoing treatment with fixed orthodontic appliances. Twice-daily (1-0-1) intake of probiotic lozenges (Limosilactobacillus reuteri) during the first three months after the placement of the fixed appliance. The intake begins on the day the fixed appliance is placed.

Adolescents (age 12–17) undergoing treatment with fixed orthodontic appliances. Twice-daily (1-0-1) intake of control lozenges (without probiotics) during the first three months after the placement of the fixed appliance. The intake begins on the day the fixed appliance is placed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adolescents (age 12 – 17) undergoing orthodontic treatment with fixed appliance

2. Signed informed consent und declaration of consent by the patients and their parents/legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with active periodontal disease
2. Patients who have undergone periodontal therapy within the last six months before insertion of fixed appliance 
3. Systemic or metabolic diseases that can be associated with or influence gingivitis (e.g., diabetes mellitus, active juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, leukemia, cancer) or that can affect the composition of the oral microbiome (e.g., chemotherapy, radiation therapy)
4. Use of anti-inflammatory medications (e.g., NSAIDs)
5. Obesity: Adolescents with a BMI > +2 standard deviations (SD) above the average value according to World Health Organization (WHO) for adolescents
6. Eating disorders or underweight adolescents: BMI > -2 SD under the average value according to WHO for adolescents
7. Above-average consumption of milk products defined as > 3 portions/day: > 1.2 L of milk or 1200 g of yoghurt/day (recommended daily intake by the German Nutrition Society: 1-3 portions of milk products corresponding to 250-310 g/day)
8. Allergy to ingredients of the lozenges 
9. Use of antibiotics or probiotics within the last 6 months or during the study
10. regular use of antibacterial mouth wash
11. Pregnancy
12. Smoking
13. Withdrawal of the declaration of consent by the patients or their parents/legal guardians
